description: The exact Node and npm pair a reproducible build is claimed against. `buildable` asserts that an exact source tree, with an exact lockfile, under an exact toolchain, produces an exact output — and the third of those was the one nothing declared. `engines` in package.json is a different question (will this run at all) and stays a floor; this file is the identity a build records and is measured against.
rules: One pair, named exactly. A range cannot be recorded in an artifact identity, because two builds inside the same range are two different builds and only one of them produced the output that was reviewed.

npm's resolution behaviour changes across majors and has changed within them. Declaring Node without declaring the npm it shipped with leaves the half that actually resolves the dependency graph undeclared.

Recording is unconditional; claiming is not. Every build records the toolchain it actually ran under. A build that ran under anything other than the declared pair records that honestly and cannot claim `buildable`.

A host that does not have the declared pair is not broken. It can intake, generate, verify, preview, edit and export. It cannot state a reproducible build identity, and saying so is the honest report rather than a failure to work around.
why: Node 22.23.2 is the current Jod LTS release and 10.9.8 is the npm it ships with, so the pair is what a clean `actions/setup-node` on the declared version produces without a second install step. CI reads it through .nvmrc; nothing hard-codes a version in a workflow.
consumers: .nvmrc — the version file every workflow and version manager resolves
package.json packageManager — the manager declaration a brownfield profile and a clean checkout both read
tooling/lib/toolchain.mjs — the reader, the comparison and the refusal
tooling/doctor.mjs — reports where the running host stands against the declaration
